answers.charter-meetings: The ethics and compliance committee must meet **at least four times per year** [1]. It must also meet with the audit committee at least annually [1], including jointly at least annually to review major non-financial compliance matters [3].
answers.charter-min-directors: The ethics and compliance committee must consist of **no fewer than three non-employee directors**, each of whom must meet the New York Stock Exchange standards for director independence [1].
answers.charter-term-length: Committee members are appointed by the board for **one-year terms**, on the recommendation of the directors and corporate governance committee [2]. They serve such terms as the board may determine, or until their earlier removal, resignation, or death [2].
answers.charter-financial-oversight: The audit committee has sole oversight of financial compliance, which covers accounting, auditing, financial reporting, and related investor disclosures [1]. The ethics and compliance committee has primary oversight of all other areas ("non-financial compliance"), and the two committees meet jointly at least annually to review major non-financial compliance matters [1].
answers.charter-section-name: The chair is designated by the board.
answers.redbook-report-concern: Under the Red Book, anyone, whether working for Lilly or not, can submit concerns about possible violations of laws and regulations, the Red Book, or company policies or procedures at https://speakup.lilly.com [1]. Under the Supplier Code of Business Conduct, known or suspected violations should be reported to Lilly sponsors or the Lilly Ethics & Compliance Hotline (www.lillyethics.ethicspoint.com, or call 1-800-815-2481) [3][4].
answers.redbook-values: This is not covered in the provided policy documents.
answers.redbook-last-step: The last step is **Step 5: Reflect and Learn**. It asks: What went well? What could be improved? Are there lessons to share with your team?
answers.redbook-ai-bias: The Red Book says Lilly strives to mitigate any inherent bias or discrimination in data, information, or algorithms when using Artificial Intelligence (AI). This is part of its commitment to responsible AI use, which also includes protecting against unintended applications, unintended access, and harm.
answers.redbook-investigations: Yes. Investigation details, including discipline, are treated as confidential [1].
answers.supplier-excluded-employee: Suppliers must report to Lilly **within five (5) calendar days** if one of their employees is excluded or restricted in any way from doing business with any government [1][2].
answers.supplier-death-report: A known or suspected death must be reported **immediately (within 24 hours of receipt)** [2][3]. In the US, report it by calling The Lilly Answers Center (TLAC) at 1.800.LillyRx (1.800.545.5979) or by using an alternative reporting method as determined by the Lilly component [2][3].
answers.supplier-hotline-number: The Lilly Ethics & Compliance Hotline phone number is **1-800-815-2481**. It can also be reached online at www.lillyethics.ethicspoint.com.
answers.supplier-cooperative-learning: This is not covered in the provided policy documents.
answers.supplier-impaired: No. Under the Lilly Supplier Code of Business Conduct, "we ensure that we are not impaired with drugs or alcohol while at work so that we can be fully engaged" [2]. This is part of the commitment to "bring our full selves to work each day" [2].
answers.supplier-adverse-event: Report any known or suspected death or suspect product immediately (within 24 hours of receipt), and any other adverse event or product complaint within one business day. Outside the US, select your location from the globe link in the upper right corner of Lilly.com, then click "Contact" or "Contact Us" in the top menu bar to access the appropriate local reporting method.
answers.retaliation: No. Lilly does not tolerate retaliation for reporting inappropriate conduct, preventing unlawful practices, or participating in an investigation, and it takes appropriate measures to prevent retaliation against people who make reports [1]. The Red Book also states that Lilly will not tolerate acts of retaliation against those who speak up, even anonymously [2].
answers.supplier-purchasing: Before purchasing goods or services, authorization from procurement and appropriate supporting documentation are required [4]. More broadly, suppliers must have appropriate authority and secure the required Lilly approvals before acquiring or committing Lilly resources or disbursing Lilly funds [4].
answers.supplier-gifts-on-behalf: Not without permission. Lilly does not allow its suppliers to offer gifts or donations on Lilly's behalf **without prior written approval** [1][2].
answers.supplier-current-version: The most recent version in the provided excerpts is **V15.0** (©2025, Eli Lilly and Company). An earlier Version 13.0 (©2021) also appears, but the excerpts do not explicitly say which version is current.
